feedback: Approved to race. The candidate is valid and changes only two controller values from iteration 2, the best raced design (600.62): base_speed 1.4 to 1.3 and kd 0.7 to 0.8. Geometry, kp 3.0, ki 0.05, sensor_weights and line_loss are unchanged. Iteration 2 showed that the oval finishes 20/20 at a mean of 1.94 s, so a drop to 1.3 should still finish inside 3 s, though the margin is smaller than before. The s-bend finished 13/20, and every failure came from going off track. The slalom finished 0/20 with max_error 0.0638 against the 0.06 m limit and about 1 line-loss event per run. Those are the failures this change targets. Because two variables change together, the race will not show which one helped. Read the result by track. If the oval finish rate falls below 1.0, or its completion_time rises above about 2.7 s, return base_speed to 1.4 and keep kd 0.8. If the slalom progress rises but it still goes off track with max_error above 0.06, try kp 2.6 at base_speed 1.2 next, which lowers the corner gain and the speed together. If the slalom line_loss_events fall but max_error stays above 0.06, raise kd to 0.9 with base_speed 1.3. Do not change geometry until the controller question is settled, since the forward sensor shift and mass 0.6 kg helped in iteration 2.
requested_changes: If the oval finish rate drops below 1.0 or its completion_time rises above about 2.7 s, set base_speed back to 1.4 and keep kd 0.8. Iteration 2 oval finished 20/20 at a mean of 1.94 s at base_speed 1.4.

If the slalom still ends off track with max_error above 0.06 (iteration 2: 0.0638, 0/20 finishes), try kp 2.6 with base_speed 1.2, which lowers both corner gain and speed. Speed is the main suspected driver of bend drift.

If the slalom line_loss_events fall but max_error stays above 0.06, raise kd from 0.8 to 0.9 with base_speed 1.3. Iteration 2 showed about 1 line-loss event per slalom run, and oval steering_oscillation was 0.25, well under the 0.3 concern.
